gloss: wishes of the deceased; dying wish

definitions.gloss: wishes of the deceased; dying wish
definitions.explanation: What a person who has died wanted or intended to do, especially the aims that others then carry on for them.

examples.english: To carry on my father's wishes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{故人|こじん}→故人：02807_kojin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遺志|いし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧、⟦{葬儀|そうぎ}→葬儀：15337_sougi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{行|おこな}われた→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: In accordance with the wishes of the deceased, the funeral was held with family only.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{亡|な}くなった→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧⟦{恩師|おんし}→恩師：12598_onshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遺志|いし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け{継|つ}いで→受け継ぐ：06700_uketsugu⟧、⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: She carried on the wishes of her late teacher and founded a school.

notes:
A written, respectful word, common in obituaries, funeral notices and news. The phrase {遺志|いし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{継|つ}ぐ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ (to carry on someone's legacy) is the most frequent use.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遺志|いし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{継|つ}ぐ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ / ⟦{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ→受け継ぐ：06700_uketsugu⟧: to carry on someone's wishes
- ⟦{故人|こじん}→故人：02807_kojin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遺志|いし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧: in accordance with the wishes of the deceased
- {遺志|いし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{尊重|そんちょう}する→尊重する：17456_sonchousuru⟧: to respect the wishes of the deceased

WATCH OUT:
- ⟦{意志|いし}→意志：01712_ishi⟧ (will, volition), ⟦{意思|いし}→意思：12742_ishi⟧ (intention) and ⟦{医師|いし}→医師：11851_ishi⟧ (doctor) share the reading
- ⟦{遺言|ゆいごん}→遺言：10896_yuigon⟧: a will, last words — the actual statement, while {遺志|いし} is the intention behind it
